Steam, oil, and eventually electric lamps replaced whale oil and other fuels, while automated mechanisms rotated the heavy lens assemblies.

Today, modern lighthouses incorporate GPS technology, radar reflectors, and radio beacons alongside their traditional visual signals. Many historic lighthouses have been preserved as museums and tourist attractions, their keepers replaced by automated systems. resulting in two high tides each day. The sun also exerts a gravitational force, though its greater distance makes its effect
roughly half that of the moon's. When the sun, moon, and Earth align during full and new moons, their combined
gravitational forces produce spring tides, characterized by higher high tides and lower low tides. Conversely, during
the first and third quarters of the moon, the sun and moon work against each other, leading to neap tides with smaller
differences between high and low water. Local geography significantly shapes tidal patterns, where bays and shelves can amplify fluctuations while open
oceans see less variation. Beyond moving water, tides shape coastlines, influence marine life, and have historically been harnessed for

fishing and energy generation.

patterns, where bays and shelves can amplify fluctuations while open oceans see less variation. Beyond moving water, tides shape coast

lines, influence marine life, and have historically been harnessed for fishing and energy generation.
